title: observability: token/kv metrics + tracing dashboard and alert tuning
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: token-level cost/latency and KV cache behavior are critical signals for optimizing inference cost and tail latency. Existing dashboards surfaced aggregate per-request metrics but lacked token-level breakdowns and KV-cache-specific traces/metrics, which made it hard to diagnose regressions after the recent batching/kv-cache refactor.

What this PR does: single continuous description string with the following changes: 1) Adds a Grafana dashboard (observability/dashboards/token-kv-overview.json) that groups token-level cost, per-token latency distribution, KV cache hit/miss rates, and allocation by model variant. 2) Introduces new aggregated Prometheus metrics with reduced cardinality (redwood_inference_tokens_total{bucket,model_variant}, redwood_kvcache_hits_total, redwood_kvcache_misses_total, redwood_kvcache_hit_ratio) and histograms for per-token latency (redwood_token_latency_seconds_bucket) to enable p50/p95/p99 analysis without high-cardinality labels. 3) Adds tracing tags to runtime spans (kv_cache.hit, batching.batch_size, model_variant, seq_len_estimate) and an improved span for KV cache lookups to capture hit/miss + key size. 4) Updates alert rules: tunes the KV cache miss-rate alert threshold and introduces a new alert for token latency p99 regression compared to a rolling baseline. 5) Adds documentation + runbook snippets for diagnosing common causes (cold KV cache, fragmentation, kernel fallback). 6) Includes unit + integration tests for metrics naming/registration and a small e2e smoke test for the dashboard JSON to validate templating variables.

Implementation notes: - To avoid cardinality explosion we only tag model_variant and bucketed sequence length (seq_len_bucket: short|medium|long) on token histograms. The PR includes a helper in observability/metrics/cardinality_helper.go used by both runtime and dedicated exporters. - Tracing tags are added behind a feature flag (FEATURE_OBS_TOKEN_TRACE) to control rollout; flag defaults to on for canary. - Alert tuning used production traffic sampling from 2026-01 to compute baselines; thresholds are conservative to avoid noise during the rollout.

Testing: CI initially failed due to a flaky prometheus exporter unit test (race on registry reset) — fixed by serializing registry initialization in tests. All integration tests (metrics + tracing mocks) pass locally and in CI after rerun. Grafana JSON validated with grafonnet linter.

Backwards compatibility: Metric names are additive; no existing metric was removed. Alerts are additive/adjusted and documented in release notes.

Action items after merge: - Monitor new alert channels for 72 hours and revert feature flag if noise appears. - Ops to provision the dashboard in the production Grafana workspace (dashboard UID included in files).

Related: ENG-8421 (improve observability for KV cache), ENG-8470 (kludge: batching refactor followups).

review_comments: Aisha Khan: Please reduce the cardinality on model_variant for per-token histograms; we've seen OOMs previously when variants proliferate.
Maya Patel (author): Reduced model_variant to only a sanitized 'model_family' and added seq_len_bucket to preserve signal without cardinality explosion.
Tom Rivera: The new alert for token-p99 regression looks promising — can we use a rolling baseline and mute alerts if the sampling window is below a threshold?
Maya Patel (author): Implemented a rolling-median baseline and added a minimum sample count check before firing (token_metrics.sample_count > 1000).
Lin Chen: Minor nit: prefer using the existing metric registration helper in observability/prometheus/registry.go rather than custom logic in metrics_exports.go
Maya Patel (author): Switched to the shared registry helper; updated tests accordingly.
Aisha Khan: Approved after the cardinality changes and tests pass.
Tom Rivera: Approved — please follow-up with Ops for dashboard provisioning.

release_notes: Add token-level cost/latency and KV cache observability: new Grafana dashboard, Prometheus metrics, tracing tags, and tuned alerts to detect token-p99 regressions and high KV miss-rates.
